chapter: Portraits from Hemphill to Getz, and the bebop question
title: Ahmad Jamal's organ and bassist Eddie Calhoun
summary: Horace bought Jamal's compact keyboard instrument, used it with the Billy Williams Revue. Bassist Eddie Calhoun, whom Horace taught to read, replaced Crosby and left for Erroll Garner.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Well, right downstairs in my basement now I've got Ahmad Jamal's organo.
Yeah, he sold it to me.

He didn't like it, and it began to be the rage around Chicago, and I -- I tried a little of the Strand where I was playing with my group, that at this Grand Ballroom (Unaudible), and it worked out real good. We -- I had a little keyboard, you know, made, not quite as big as the piano and I pressed these -- you know the story -- and that little we had too bar that would go behind the piano keyboard (Unaudible), but -- and I had a guy playing bass with me then that took Crosby's place, that was a legend. I taught him how to read, and after I had taught him to read, please believe me, after he'd been with me for three years, and I mean he could read -- he went with guess who? Erroll Garner, who didn't need it.

And I met him one time in New York, and he says, 'now that's Little Smack.' He said, 'Here's the man that taught me how to read on my bass, taught me how to do everything,' he said. 'I wind up going with a guy I don't have to read music.' Isn't that funny, you know?

So -- real funny -- and he was quite a bass player. Eddie Calhoun was -- and he was quite a comedian. In fact, there's a friend of mine that wrote a tune called -- I collaborated with him on that -- called Shack in Hackensack. " Real funny, you know? And Eddie used to talk this, and he and that girl vocalist, big girl -- chick she was from Birmingham, Alabama, named Jean Cunningham. They used to do this thing and played it up. He was a little runt, and she was tall and used to stand under him. And besides doing (inaudible) Comedy old have he had his bass out (inaudible) and play. It was a good thing. He took Crosby's place, and he did a good job, and he was the one that told me that Jamal wanted to get rid of this oregana, and it was quite popular in Chicago at that time and I was anxious had a chance to get it.

So he had one already made up that you didn't have to bother with the piano, putting that bar behind. He had the regular keyboard that was sawed off, up to only so many octaves. And it was all a compact unit, you know. I've got it downstairs.
And I played it, even with the Billy Williams Revue, that thing has been on the stage of the Riviera in Las Vegas. I had it with the Billy Williams Revue, and I had it up in Montecello, New York, at
Grossinger's and Brown's and all those, so that thing has been in all the places. It served the purpose at that time. So I just keep it now as a -- what do you call it --
